answerNotes.BREAD: Bread may be a whole loaf or pieces cut from it. A loaf is counted as a whole, while a slice is one flat portion.
answerNotes.CINNAMON: Cinnamon comes from bark. It is sold in rolled sticks as well as ground into a fine powder.
answerNotes.FLOUR: Flour is ground grain used in baking. The fine powder is different from whole kernels even when both come from the same crop.
answerNotes.EGG: A hen's egg has a shell, white, and yolk. Recipes sometimes use only one inner part rather than the whole egg.
answerNotes.PAN: Pan is a broad kitchen word. A frying pan is used on a stove, while a loaf pan holds dough or batter in the oven.
answerNotes.BAKE: Baking uses dry heat in an oven. Boiling instead cooks food in bubbling liquid.
answerNotes.OVEN: An oven cooks with heat surrounding the food. That differs from the direct bottom heat under a pan on a stovetop.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.FALL: Fall is the usual American word for autumn. Both name the season after summer and before winter.
